title: Executive Turntable: Sphere & Fender Name New Chief Communications Officers
summary: This week's Executive Turntable column includes Chris Palmer's elevation at Triple Tiger Records, Timo Hoffman joining Frontiers Label Group and more music industry promotions and hires.
contentText:
Sphere Entertainment Co. has named Karen Laureano-Rikardsen as the company’s new global head of corporate marketing and communications. Reporting to Sphere’s president and chief operating officer, Jennifer Koester , Laureano-Rikardsen will be based in New York City.

“As we continue to expand Sphere’s presence and bring our next-generation immersive entertainment experiences to audiences around the world, it is critical that we continue to tell our story in compelling and impactful ways,” Koester said in a statement. “Karen brings a strong combination of global marketing and communications experience, sound judgement and proven leadership in high-profile environments. She will play a vital role in shaping how we communicate our vision and innovation.”

Prior to joining the company, Laureano-Rikardsen served as chief communications and marketing officer at Cantor Fitzgerald.

Since opening its doors on Sept. 29, Sphere Las Vegas has hosted residencies from the likes of U2, Phish, Dead & Company and more. Upcoming events at the venue include Backstreet Boys, Carín León and Metallica. Sphere Entertainment plans to complete a 20,000 capacity venue in Yas Island, Abu Dhabi by the end of 2029, and has plans for a 6,000 capacity location in National Harbor, Maryland.

“Throughout my career, I have worked with global organizations to strengthen corporate reputations and develop communications strategies that drive business growth and meaningful engagement with audiences,” Laureano-Rikardsen said in a statement. “Sphere is a unique company at the intersection of technology, storytelling and live entertainment, and I look forward to working alongside the talented team of creatives, engineers, technologists and business leaders to help fuel the company’s continued expansion.” — Ariel King
